source.title_on_document: GenAI-driven storytelling on senior secondary students' Generative AI literacy and writing skills: A mixed-methods research

supplement.holds: The document refers to no supplement or online appendix. No table of means, SDs, t-tests, ANCOVA results or Cohen's d is printed anywhere, although Section 3.6 says these were computed.

paper_design_summary: 76 Form 4 and Form 5 students at one Hong Kong secondary school were split into an experimental group (n = 38) that took a five-week, ten-hour GenAI-driven digital storytelling workshop and a control group (n = 38) that continued conventional English lessons without AI tools; the paper says assignment was by simple random sampling but also calls the design quasi-experimental. Before and immediately after the intervention, both groups wrote a story without AI help, scored with a creative writing rubric (word usage, narrative structure, creativity; total out of 15), and completed AI literacy and writing anxiety questionnaires; nine experimental students were interviewed.

studies.label: Classroom experiment: GenAI-driven storytelling workshop vs conventional English lessons (Hong Kong secondary school)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Experimental group (five-week GenAI-driven storytelling workshop) vs control group (conventional English lessons without AI tools)
assignment.quote: Participants were assigned to either the experimental or control group through a process of simple random sampling.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 6 (journal p. 84), Section 3.3; also abstract PDF p. 1 (p. 79): '76 students who were randomly assigned to control and experimental groups'. Same Section 3.3 calls it 'a pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design'. The unit of assignment (individual students or classes) is not stated.

arms.name: Experimental group
arms.description: Five-week, ten-hour GenAI-driven storytelling workshop (two 60-minute sessions per week in the school computer lab), following a 5-step GenAI storytelling model with instructor-designed prompt banks; 18 Form 4 and 20 Form 5 students.

arms.name: Control group
arms.description: Continued with conventional English lessons without exposure to any AI tools.

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper gives 76 students divided 38/38 (PDF p. 5, p. 6 Figure 1, p. 8 Section 4.1) and never states how many completed the post-test or entered each analysis.
participants.who: Form 4 and Form 5 (senior secondary) students at a Band 3 government-funded secondary school in a public housing district serving socioeconomically disadvantaged students; low digital and GenAI literacy.
participants.quote: This study was conducted at a Band 3 secondary school in Hong Kong and involved a total of 76 students from Form 4 and Form 5.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (journal p. 83), Section 3.1; PDF p. 6 (p. 84), Figure 1; PDF p. 8 (p. 86), Section 4.1

ai_tool.name_model: not_stated (unnamed 'GenAI tools' for text, visuals, and music)
ai_tool.how_used: During the workshop only: brainstorming, prompt crafting and outline building with GenAI text tools (week 2), creating visuals (week 3), generating AI music (week 4), and final story editing and presentation (week 5), supported by instructor-designed prompt banks (Table 1, PDF p. 7; Section 3.2, PDF p. 6). The scored pre- and post-test stories were written with no AI help (Figure 1, PDF p. 6).

task.description: Storytelling (narrative writing) task completed without AI help at pre-test and post-test, scored with the Creative Writing Assessment Rubric (Carey et al., 2022) on word usage, narrative structure, and creativity.
task.duration: Test duration not stated; intervention five weeks, two 60-minute sessions per week (ten hours).

outcomes.name: Creativity dimension of the Creative Writing Assessment Rubric

outcomes.measure_detail: Rubric-based performance assessment (Carey et al., 2022) of students' writing samples; who scored the stories, whether raters were blind to group, and inter-rater reliability are not stated (rater type coded expert_raters by assumption). Score range of the dimension not stated; the total of three dimensions is out of 15.
outcomes.delay: Post-test administered immediately after the five-week intervention (Section 3.3, PDF p. 6)

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1: the paper states random assignment (abstract p. 79; Section 3.3 p. 84, 'simple random sampling') but in the same section calls the design 'pretest-posttest quasi-experimental', and it does not say whether students or intact classes were assigned; the control group 'continued with conventional English lessons'. Criterion 2: 76 students assigned 38/38; no attrition or analyzed count is reported, so the 76 is the assigned count. Criterion 3: the creativity dimension of a writing rubric is scored on stories written without AI after the intervention (after_ai). Note that no between-group statistic is printed for any writing outcome.

one_line_finding: In the experimental group the mean overall writing score on a no-AI story task rose from 3.34 to 8.71 out of 15 after a five-week GenAI storytelling workshop, with gains on creativity shown only in Figure 3, while the control group showed no significant change; no between-group statistic is printed (PDF pp. 11-12, journal pp. 89-90).
open_questions: Was assignment by individual student or by intact class, and is the design truly randomized given the 'quasi-experimental' label (p. 84)?
Who scored the stories (teacher-author or independent raters), were they blind to group and time, and what was inter-rater reliability?
How many students completed the post-test in each group (analyzed n)?
Control-group means, SDs, and the ANCOVA and Cohen's d results that Section 3.6 says were computed are not printed; they would need to come from the author.
notes: Other outcomes are self-reports and are not listed: AI Literacy Questionnaire (four domains; experimental pre vs post in Figure 2, p. 88, p < .001) and Writing Anxiety Scale (three subdimensions; Figure 4, p. 91, p < .001). Interviews with 9 experimental students (Figure 1) are qualitative. Figure 3 is titled 'Experimental Group Comparison' and shows no control-group bars. The paper lists four research questions although the text says three. Journal page = PDF page + 78.
